title: OPM moves to allow agencies to promote workers faster
summary: Officials said the nearly 80-year-old requirement that federal employees serve in their current positions for at least one year before they may be promoted is “outdated.”

title: Bipartisan IRS whistleblower reform bill gains momentum in Senate after House approval
summary: The IRS said that it has collected around $7.5 billion due to whistleblowers since 2007.

title: GSA joins White House’s fraud prevention task force
summary: The agency said it will support the unit’s efforts by identifying waste, fraud and abuse across government contracting programs.

title: Tech Force set out to hire 1,000 technologists last year. It’s onboarded 10 so far
summary: The effort is meant to infuse the government with young engineers, cyber and data workers. It follows the loss of almost 20,000 technology workers through the Trump administration’s efforts to downsize the workforce last year.

title: Lacking data policy is more than a research problem, it's a government performance problem
summary: COMMENTARY | The ongoing erosion of the federal statistical system, marked by broken time series and a workforce crisis, threatens government capacity to serve the public.

title: Citing legal requirement, senator wants a designated inspector general to provide oversight of Iran war
summary: The Council of Inspectors General on Integrity and Efficiency is required to select an IG to oversee reviews when a military “overseas contingency operation” surpasses 60 days.

title: What retiring feds should do before asking for help
summary: Clear timelines, complete records and focused questions can make retirement problems easier to resolve, especially as agencies face mounting workloads.

title: Top White House cyber policy official to soon depart
summary: Alexandra Seymour currently serves as principal deputy assistant national cyber director for policy in the Office of the National Cyber Director.

title: Labor oversight official faces ethics complaint for apparent congressional campaign moves
summary: While Anthony D'Esposito decided not to run for his former House seat, federal employees are not permitted to be candidates in partisan elections, which includes taking preliminary actions for a campaign.

title: House draft of defense policy bill leaves some of Trump admin’s top priorities unfunded
summary: The draft bill doesn’t include reconciliation dollars.

title: Someone robbed the SEC during the shutdown
summary: An individual has been arrested, but the stolen materials have not been recovered.

title: Supreme Court rejects lower court bid to review immigration judge gag order
summary: Justices reversed an appeals court decision that would have greenlit a fact-finding expedition into whether President Trump had effectively nullified review of personnel policies under the 1978 Civil Service Reform Act.

title: Disability advocates sue over website accessibility delays
summary: The National Federation of the Blind sued the departments of Justice and Health and Human Services after a rule requiring government websites to be accessible was delayed for a year.

title: They were told they’d move on. A year later, many fired federal employees say they haven’t been able to
summary: A group of former federal probationary employees surveyed more than 300 of their fired colleagues to assess their job searches, mental health and several other topics.

title: OPM proposes requiring all feds to sign an NDA
summary: Experts warned the measure, when combined with the federal HR agency’s new power to target employees’ suitability for federal employment, creates a new pathway for Trump administration officials to purge those deemed insufficiently loyal to the president.

title: Beekeepers are losing a key USDA backstop at the worst possible time
summary: As colony losses mount and pollinator research faces broader cuts, the planned closure of the Beltsville Bee Research Lab threatens a critical line of support for the nation’s food system.

title: FAA surges medical staff after whistleblower alleges issues with certifying pilots and controllers
summary: Hundreds of pilots may have been flying without proper medical clearance, the whistleblower had alleged.

title: Congress must tie any USPS bailout to real reform
summary: COMMENTARY | Before Congress delivers any financial relief, it should demand enforceable guardrails on service, prices and oversight.

title: The White House is ordering agencies to place its new app on all employees’ government phones
summary: The newly created, often overtly political app places the Trump administration into unprecedented and “dangerous” territory, IT experts say.

title: Agency leaders back GSA bid for full access to federal building repair funds
summary: Officials argued that GSA’s deferred maintenance backlog has increased to an estimated $26 billion, in part, because Congress puts annual restrictions on amounts the agency can spend from the Federal Buildings Fund.

title: Gabbard to resign as director of national intelligence, citing husband’s health
summary: Her exit marks the end of a 16-month tenure overseeing the nation’s spy agencies, where the former Democratic congresswoman and 2020 presidential candidate sought to reshape ODNI around Trump’s priorities.

title: NTEU asks Trump administration to ease telework rules as gas prices spike
summary: The union also called for an increase in gas reimbursement rates as the president’s war against Iran continues to disrupt the world’s oil supply.

title: Ryan Donaghy returns to CISA as first chief operating officer
summary: Donaghy previously served in acting leadership roles across two of the agency’s divisions and moved to the Transportation Security Administration in October.
